transcript.text: Thank you all for joining this pre-conference review. As you know, our first case-management conference is in three weeks, and I need to approve our draft litigation plan before we finalize it. The current draft preserves both asserted claims — claim 7 and claim 12 — seeks broad technical discovery, and permits source-code production under the opposing party's proposed protective order. Before I sign off, I need each of you to report any facts that should change this draft plan. Specifically, I need to know: Are there any validity issues with either claim 7 or claim 12? Is there any reason to narrow or expand the discovery scope? And are there any concerns with accepting the opposing party's protective order as drafted? Please share what you know.

transcript.text: I need to flag a significant validity issue with claim 7. Yesterday, while reviewing a newly indexed prior-art collection, I found a published 2016 software implementation that anticipates every limitation of claim 7. Under our litigation policy, this requires claim 7 to be withdrawn from the asserted-claims strategy. I have not yet revised the draft plan because the prior-art collection was indexed after the plan circulated. My separate review found no equivalent anticipation of claim 12, so claim 12 should remain in the strategy. This means the draft plan needs to be updated to withdraw claim 7 and to limit discovery to material relevant to the surviving claim 12.

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious concern with accepting the opposing party's proposed protective order as drafted. This week I confirmed with the engineering security team that the proposed protective order is inadequate for our source code. It allows two named employees of the opposing party to access produced code, but our board-approved security policy requires source-code access to be limited to outside counsel and independent experts who have signed enhanced source-code acknowledgments. I had not yet updated the litigation plan because the security team's confirmation arrived after our last legal-team meeting. The draft plan needs to be revised to reject the opposing party's protective order as drafted and to require a protective order that complies with our board-approved source-code security policy before any source-code production occurs.
